response.answer:
I’ll keep **Combined Honours in Biochemistry and Forensic Science** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor of Science  
- **Duration:** Four years  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Locations:** Burnaby Campus and UBC Vancouver  
- **Institutions:** Joint UBC/BCIT program  
- **Status:** Active  
- **Completion requirement:** 132 credits  

### Curriculum highlights

**Year 1 – UBC**
- Required: **BIOL 112 — UBC-BIOL-112 — Biology of the Cell**
- Required: **CHEM 123 — UBC-CHEM-123 — UBC-CHEM-111 — UBC-CHEM-121 — UBC-CHEM-141 — Principles of Chemistry 2**
- Required: **SCIE 113 — UBC-SCIE-113 — First-Year Seminar in Science**
- Chemistry alternative: **CHEM 121 — Principles of Chemistry**, **CHEM 111 — Principles of Chemistry**, or **CHEM 141 — Principles of Chemistry**, together with **CHEM 123 — Principles of Chemistry 2**
- Data science alternative: **DSCI 100 — UBC-DSCI-100 — Introduction to Data Science** or **CPSC 103 — UBC-CPSC-103 — Introduction to Systematic Program Design**
- Calculus alternative: **MATH 100 — UBC-MATH-100 — UBC-MATH-102 — UBC-MATH-104 — Differential Calculus**, **MATH 102 — Differential Calculus**, or **MATH 104 — Differential Calculus**

**Year 2 – BCIT**
- **COMM 7200 — Report Writing and Workplace Communication for Forensic Investigation**
- **FSCT 7320 — Introduction to Forensic Science**
- **LIBS 7020 — Bioethics**

**Year 2 – UBC**
- Required: **BIOC 203 — UBC-BIOC-203 — Fundamentals of Biochemistry**
- **BIOL 200 — UBC-BIOL-200 — Fundamentals of Cell Biology**
- **BIOL 234 — UBC-BIOL-234 — Fundamentals of Genetics**
- **CHEM 203 — UBC-CHEM-203 — Introduction to UBC-CHEM-213 — Organic Chemistry**
- **CHEM 211 — UBC-CHEM-211 — Introduction to Chemical Analysis**
- **CHEM 213 — Organic Chemistry**
- **CHEM 245 — UBC-CHEM-245 — Intermediate Organic Chemistry Lab**
- Computing/statistics alternative: **STAT 201 — UBC-STAT-201 — Statistical Inference for Data Science** or **CPSC 203 — UBC-CPSC-203 — Programming, Problem Solving, and Algorithms**

**Year 3 – BCIT**
- **FSCT 8150 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Theory**
- **FSCT 8155 — Forensic Biology: Evidence Recovery**
- **FSCT 8370 — Quality Assurance for Forensic Science**
- **FSCT 8371 — Business Management for Forensic Science**
- Elective pool includes **FSCT 7310 — Crime and Incident Scene Investigation**, **FSCT 7910 — Research Methodology and Measurement Models**, **FSCT 8230 — The Medicolegal Aspects of Alcohol**, **FSCT 8240 — Forensic Toxicology**, and **FSCT 8320 — The Science of Fingerprints - Theory**

**Year 3 – UBC**
- **BIOC 301 — UBC-BIOC-301 — Biochemistry Laboratory**
- **BIOC 303 — UBC-BIOC-303 — Molecular Biochemistry**
- **BIOL 335 — UBC-BIOL-335 — Molecular Genetics**

**Year 4 – BCIT**
- **FSCT 7009 — Law for Forensic Science**
- **FSCT 7010 — The Expert Witness: Prepared for Court**
- **FSCT 8156 — Instrumental Analysis for Forensic Chemistry**
- **FSCT 8160 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Applications**

**Year 4 – UBC**
You choose one of the stored Biochemistry pathways:

- **Path 1:** **BIOC 449 — UBC-BIOC-449 — Honours Thesis** plus 3 credits of advanced Biochemistry electives.
- **Path 2:** **BIOC 420 — UBC-BIOC-420 — Advanced Biochemical Techniques** plus 6 credits of advanced Biochemistry electives.

The advanced Biochemistry options include **BIOC 402 — UBC-BIOC-402 — Proteins: Structure and Function**, **BIOC 403 — UBC-BIOC-403 — Enzymology**, **BIOC 410 — UBC-BIOC-410 — Nucleic Acid: Structure and Function**, **BIOC 421 — UBC-BIOC-421 — Recombinant DNA Techniques**, **BIOC 430 — UBC-BIOC-430 — Advanced Topics in Protein Biochemistry**, **BIOC 440 — UBC-BIOC-440 — Concepts in Molecular Biology**, **BIOC 450 — UBC-BIOC-450 — Membrane Biochemistry**, **BIOC 460 — UBC-BIOC-460 — Advanced Techniques in Biochemistry**, and **BIOC 470 — UBC-BIOC-470 — Biochemistry and Society: Current Issues**.

Other Year 4 UBC options include **BIOL 301 — UBC-BIOL-301 — Biomathematics**, **BIOL 336 — UBC-BIOL-336 — Fundamentals of Evolutionary Biology**, **BIOL 462 — UBC-BIOL-462 — Ecological Plant Biochemistry**, **CPSC 330 — UBC-CPSC-330 — Applied Machine Learning**, **MEDG 421 — UBC-MEDG-421 — Genetics and Cell Biology of Cancer**, **MICB 405 — UBC-MICB-405 — Bioinformatics**, and **PCTH 325 — UBC-PCTH-325 — Rational Basis of Drug Therapy**.

### Admissions information
The stored program record includes:
- A UBC pathway with a minimum GPA of **76%**, changing to **70% for September 2026**, plus specified Chemistry, Communication, Biology, and calculus preparation.
- A transfer pathway requiring two terms of Chemistry with lab, and one term each of Biology, English, and differential calculus.
- A criminal record check as an entrance requirement.
- Optional co-op placement.

The stored admissions record says applications are made through UBC Science/UBC Admissions, followed by an application for the specialization in June. Timing details for the criminal record check are not verified in the available data.

[Program information and source](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/)

I’ll keep **Combined Honours in Biochemistry and Forensic Science** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor of Science  
- **Duration:** Four years  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Locations:** Burnaby Campus and UBC Vancouver  
- **Institutions:** Joint UBC/BCIT program  
- **Status:** Active  
- **Completion requirement:** 132 credits  

### Curriculum highlights

**Year 1 – UBC**
- Required: **BIOL 112 — Biology of the Cell**
- Required: **CHEM 123 — Principles of Chemistry 2**
- Required: **SCIE 113 — First-Year Seminar in Science**
- Chemistry alternative: **CHEM 121 — Principles of Chemistry**, **CHEM 111 — Principles of Chemistry**, or **CHEM 141 — Principles of Chemistry**, together with **CHEM 123 — Principles of Chemistry 2**
- Data science alternative: **DSCI 100 — Introduction to Data Science** or **CPSC 103 — Introduction to Systematic Program Design**
- Calculus alternative: **MATH 100 — Differential Calculus**, **MATH 102 — Differential Calculus**, or **MATH 104 — Differential Calculus**

**Year 2 – BCIT**
- **COMM 7200 — Report Writing and Workplace Communication for Forensic Investigation**
- **FSCT 7320 — Introduction to Forensic Science**
- **LIBS 7020 — Bioethics**

**Year 2 – UBC**
- Required: **BIOC 203 — Fundamentals of Biochemistry**
- **BIOL 200 — Fundamentals of Cell Biology**
- **BIOL 234 — Fundamentals of Genetics**
- **CHEM 203 — Introduction to Organic Chemistry**
- **CHEM 211 — Introduction to Chemical Analysis**
- **CHEM 213 — Organic Chemistry**
- **CHEM 245 — Intermediate Organic Chemistry Lab**
- Computing/statistics alternative: **STAT 201 — Statistical Inference for Data Science** or **CPSC 203 — Programming, Problem Solving, and Algorithms**

**Year 3 – BCIT**
- **FSCT 8150 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Theory**
- **FSCT 8155 — Forensic Biology: Evidence Recovery**
- **FSCT 8370 — Quality Assurance for Forensic Science**
- **FSCT 8371 — Business Management for Forensic Science**
- Elective pool includes **FSCT 7310 — Crime and Incident Scene Investigation**, **FSCT 7910 — Research Methodology and Measurement Models**, **FSCT 8230 — The Medicolegal Aspects of Alcohol**, **FSCT 8240 — Forensic Toxicology**, and **FSCT 8320 — The Science of Fingerprints - Theory**

**Year 3 – UBC**
- **BIOC 301 — Biochemistry Laboratory**
- **BIOC 303 — Molecular Biochemistry**
- **BIOL 335 — Molecular Genetics**

**Year 4 – BCIT**
- **FSCT 7009 — Law for Forensic Science**
- **FSCT 7010 — The Expert Witness: Prepared for Court**
- **FSCT 8156 — Instrumental Analysis for Forensic Chemistry**
- **FSCT 8160 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Applications**

**Year 4 – UBC**
You choose one of the stored Biochemistry pathways:

- **Path 1:** **BIOC 449 — Honours Thesis** plus 3 credits of advanced Biochemistry electives.
- **Path 2:** **BIOC 420 — Advanced Biochemical Techniques** plus 6 credits of advanced Biochemistry electives.

The advanced Biochemistry options include **BIOC 402 — Proteins: Structure and Function**, **BIOC 403 — Enzymology**, **BIOC 410 — Nucleic Acid: Structure and Function**, **BIOC 421 — Recombinant DNA Techniques**, **BIOC 430 — Advanced Topics in Protein Biochemistry**, **BIOC 440 — Concepts in Molecular Biology**, **BIOC 450 — Membrane Biochemistry**, **BIOC 460 — Advanced Techniques in Biochemistry**, and **BIOC 470 — Biochemistry and Society: Current Issues**.

Other Year 4 UBC options include **BIOL 301 — Biomathematics**, **BIOL 336 — Fundamentals of Evolutionary Biology**, **BIOL 462 — Ecological Plant Biochemistry**, **CPSC 330 — Applied Machine Learning**, **MEDG 421 — Genetics and Cell Biology of Cancer**, **MICB 405 — Bioinformatics**, and **PCTH 325 — Rational Basis of Drug Therapy**.

### Admissions information
The stored program record includes:
- A UBC pathway with a minimum GPA of **76%**, changing to **70% for September 2026**, plus specified Chemistry, Communication, Biology, and calculus preparation.
- A transfer pathway requiring two terms of Chemistry with lab, and one term each of Biology, English, and differential calculus.
- A criminal record check as an entrance requirement.
- Optional co-op placement.

The stored admissions record says applications are made through UBC Science/UBC Admissions, followed by an application for the specialization in June. Timing details for the criminal record check are not verified in the available data.

[Program information and source](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/)

- **Credential:** Bachelor of Science

### Curriculum highlights

**Year 1 – UBC**
- Required: **BIOL 112 — UBC-BIOL-112 — Biology of the Cell**
- Required: **CHEM 123 — UBC-CHEM-123 — UBC-CHEM-111 — UBC-CHEM-121 — UBC-CHEM-141 — Principles of Chemistry 2**
- Required: **SCIE 113 — UBC-SCIE-113 — First-Year Seminar in Science**
- Chemistry alternative: **CHEM 121 — Principles of Chemistry**, **CHEM 111 — Principles of Chemistry**, or **CHEM 141 — Principles of Chemistry**, together with **CHEM 123 — Principles of Chemistry 2**
- Data science alternative: **DSCI 100 — UBC-DSCI-100 — Introduction to Data Science** or **CPSC 103 — UBC-CPSC-103 — Introduction to Systematic Program Design**
- Calculus alternative: **MATH 100 — UBC-MATH-100 — UBC-MATH-102 — UBC-MATH-104 — Differential Calculus**, **MATH 102 — Differential Calculus**, or **MATH 104 — Differential Calculus**

**Year 2 – BCIT**
- **COMM 7200 — Report Writing and Workplace Communication for Forensic Investigation**
- **FSCT 7320 — Introduction to Forensic Science**
- **LIBS 7020 — Bioethics**

**Year 2 – UBC**
- Required: **BIOC 203 — UBC-BIOC-203 — Fundamentals of Biochemistry**
- **BIOL 200 — UBC-BIOL-200 — Fundamentals of Cell Biology**
- **BIOL 234 — UBC-BIOL-234 — Fundamentals of Genetics**
- **CHEM 203 — UBC-CHEM-203 — Introduction to UBC-CHEM-213 — Organic Chemistry**
- **CHEM 211 — UBC-CHEM-211 — Introduction to Chemical Analysis**
- **CHEM 213 — Organic Chemistry**
- **CHEM 245 — UBC-CHEM-245 — Intermediate Organic Chemistry Lab**
- Computing/statistics alternative: **STAT 201 — UBC-STAT-201 — Statistical Inference for Data Science** or **CPSC 203 — UBC-CPSC-203 — Programming, Problem Solving, and Algorithms**

- **FSCT 8150 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Theory**
- **FSCT 8155 — Forensic Biology: Evidence Recovery**
- **FSCT 8370 — Quality Assurance for Forensic Science**
- **FSCT 8371 — Business Management for Forensic Science**
- Elective pool includes **FSCT 7310 — Crime and Incident Scene Investigation**, **FSCT 7910 — Research Methodology and Measurement Models**, **FSCT 8230 — The Medicolegal Aspects of Alcohol**, **FSCT 8240 — Forensic Toxicology**, and **FSCT 8320 — The Science of Fingerprints - Theory**

**Year 3 – UBC**
- **BIOC 301 — UBC-BIOC-301 — Biochemistry Laboratory**
- **BIOC 303 — UBC-BIOC-303 — Molecular Biochemistry**
- **BIOL 335 — UBC-BIOL-335 — Molecular Genetics**

**Year 4 – BCIT**
- **FSCT 7009 — Law for Forensic Science**
- **FSCT 7010 — The Expert Witness: Prepared for Court**
- **FSCT 8156 — Instrumental Analysis for Forensic Chemistry**
- **FSCT 8160 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Applications**

content.text:
The **Combined Honours in Biochemistry and Forensic Science** is a **four-year, full-time Bachelor of Science** jointly delivered by **UBC and BCIT**, with study at UBC Vancouver and BCIT’s Burnaby campus.

The program combines biochemistry, biology, chemistry, and forensic science coursework, including areas such as forensic biology, DNA analysis, instrumental analysis, and advanced biochemistry. It requires **132 credits** and includes an **optional co-op placement**.

[View the program information and source](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/)

I’ll keep **Combined Honours in Biochemistry and Forensic Science** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor of Science  
- **Duration:** Four years  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Locations:** Burnaby Campus and UBC Vancouver  
- **Institutions:** Joint UBC/BCIT program  
- **Status:** Active  
- **Completion requirement:** 132 credits  

### Curriculum highlights

**Year 1 – UBC**
- Required: **BIOL 112 — UBC-BIOL-112 — Biology of the Cell**
- Required: **CHEM 123 — UBC-CHEM-123 — UBC-CHEM-111 — UBC-CHEM-121 — UBC-CHEM-141 — Principles of Chemistry 2**
- Required: **SCIE 113 — UBC-SCIE-113 — First-Year Seminar in Science**
- Chemistry alternative: **CHEM 121 — Principles of Chemistry**, **CHEM 111 — Principles of Chemistry**, or **CHEM 141 — Principles of Chemistry**, together with **CHEM 123 — Principles of Chemistry 2**
- Data science alternative: **DSCI 100 — UBC-DSCI-100 — Introduction to Data Science** or **CPSC 103 — UBC-CPSC-103 — Introduction to Systematic Program Design**
- Calculus alternative: **MATH 100 — UBC-MATH-100 — UBC-MATH-102 — UBC-MATH-104 — Differential Calculus**, **MATH 102 — Differential Calculus**, or **MATH 104 — Differential Calculus**

**Year 2 – BCIT**
- **COMM 7200 — Report Writing and Workplace Communication for Forensic Investigation**
- **FSCT 7320 — Introduction to Forensic Science**
- **LIBS 7020 — Bioethics**

**Year 2 – UBC**
- Required: **BIOC 203 — UBC-BIOC-203 — Fundamentals of Biochemistry**
- **BIOL 200 — UBC-BIOL-200 — Fundamentals of Cell Biology**
- **BIOL 234 — UBC-BIOL-234 — Fundamentals of Genetics**
- **CHEM 203 — UBC-CHEM-203 — Introduction to UBC-CHEM-213 — Organic Chemistry**
- **CHEM 211 — UBC-CHEM-211 — Introduction to Chemical Analysis**
- **CHEM 213 — Organic Chemistry**
- **CHEM 245 — UBC-CHEM-245 — Intermediate Organic Chemistry Lab**
- Computing/statistics alternative: **STAT 201 — UBC-STAT-201 — Statistical Inference for Data Science** or **CPSC 203 — UBC-CPSC-203 — Programming, Problem Solving, and Algorithms**

**Year 3 – BCIT**
- **FSCT 8150 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Theory**
- **FSCT 8155 — Forensic Biology: Evidence Recovery**
- **FSCT 8370 — Quality Assurance for Forensic Science**
- **FSCT 8371 — Business Management for Forensic Science**
- Elective pool includes **FSCT 7310 — Crime and Incident Scene Investigation**, **FSCT 7910 — Research Methodology and Measurement Models**, **FSCT 8230 — The Medicolegal Aspects of Alcohol**, **FSCT 8240 — Forensic Toxicology**, and **FSCT 8320 — The Science of Fingerprints - Theory**

**Year 3 – UBC**
- **BIOC 301 — UBC-BIOC-301 — Biochemistry Laboratory**
- **BIOC 303 — UBC-BIOC-303 — Molecular Biochemistry**
- **BIOL 335 — UBC-BIOL-335 — Molecular Genetics**

**Year 4 – BCIT**
- **FSCT 7009 — Law for Forensic Science**
- **FSCT 7010 — The Expert Witness: Prepared for Court**
- **FSCT 8156 — Instrumental Analysis for Forensic Chemistry**
- **FSCT 8160 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Applications**

**Year 4 – UBC**
You choose one of the stored Biochemistry pathways:

- **Path 1:** **BIOC 449 — UBC-BIOC-449 — Honours Thesis** plus 3 credits of advanced Biochemistry electives.
- **Path 2:** **BIOC 420 — UBC-BIOC-420 — Advanced Biochemical Techniques** plus 6 credits of advanced Biochemistry electives.

The advanced Biochemistry options include **BIOC 402 — UBC-BIOC-402 — Proteins: Structure and Function**, **BIOC 403 — UBC-BIOC-403 — Enzymology**, **BIOC 410 — UBC-BIOC-410 — Nucleic Acid: Structure and Function**, **BIOC 421 — UBC-BIOC-421 — Recombinant DNA Techniques**, **BIOC 430 — UBC-BIOC-430 — Advanced Topics in Protein Biochemistry**, **BIOC 440 — UBC-BIOC-440 — Concepts in Molecular Biology**, **BIOC 450 — UBC-BIOC-450 — Membrane Biochemistry**, **BIOC 460 — UBC-BIOC-460 — Advanced Techniques in Biochemistry**, and **BIOC 470 — UBC-BIOC-470 — Biochemistry and Society: Current Issues**.

Other Year 4 UBC options include **BIOL 301 — UBC-BIOL-301 — Biomathematics**, **BIOL 336 — UBC-BIOL-336 — Fundamentals of Evolutionary Biology**, **BIOL 462 — UBC-BIOL-462 — Ecological Plant Biochemistry**, **CPSC 330 — UBC-CPSC-330 — Applied Machine Learning**, **MEDG 421 — UBC-MEDG-421 — Genetics and Cell Biology of Cancer**, **MICB 405 — UBC-MICB-405 — Bioinformatics**, and **PCTH 325 — UBC-PCTH-325 — Rational Basis of Drug Therapy**.

### Admissions information

- A UBC pathway with a minimum GPA of **76%**, changing to **70% for September 2026**, plus specified Chemistry, Communication, Biology, and calculus preparation.
- A transfer pathway requiring two terms of Chemistry with lab, and one term each of Biology, English, and differential calculus.
- A criminal record check as an entrance requirement.
- Optional co-op placement.

I’ll keep **Combined Honours in Biochemistry and Forensic Science** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor of Science  
- **Duration:** Four years  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Locations:** Burnaby Campus and UBC Vancouver  
- **Institutions:** Joint UBC/BCIT program  
- **Status:** Active  
- **Completion requirement:** 132 credits  

### Curriculum highlights

**Year 1 – UBC**
- Required: **BIOL 112 — UBC-BIOL-112 — Biology of the Cell**
- Required: **CHEM 123 — UBC-CHEM-123 — UBC-CHEM-111 — UBC-CHEM-121 — UBC-CHEM-141 — Principles of Chemistry 2**
- Required: **SCIE 113 — UBC-SCIE-113 — First-Year Seminar in Science**
- Chemistry alternative: **CHEM 121 — Principles of Chemistry**, **CHEM 111 — Principles of Chemistry**, or **CHEM 141 — Principles of Chemistry**, together with **CHEM 123 — Principles of Chemistry 2**
- Data science alternative: **DSCI 100 — UBC-DSCI-100 — Introduction to Data Science** or **CPSC 103 — UBC-CPSC-103 — Introduction to Systematic Program Design**
- Calculus alternative: **MATH 100 — UBC-MATH-100 — UBC-MATH-102 — UBC-MATH-104 — Differential Calculus**, **MATH 102 — Differential Calculus**, or **MATH 104 — Differential Calculus**

**Year 2 – BCIT**
- **COMM 7200 — Report Writing and Workplace Communication for Forensic Investigation**
- **FSCT 7320 — Introduction to Forensic Science**
- **LIBS 7020 — Bioethics**

**Year 2 – UBC**
- Required: **BIOC 203 — UBC-BIOC-203 — Fundamentals of Biochemistry**
- **BIOL 200 — UBC-BIOL-200 — Fundamentals of Cell Biology**
- **BIOL 234 — UBC-BIOL-234 — Fundamentals of Genetics**
- **CHEM 203 — UBC-CHEM-203 — Introduction to UBC-CHEM-213 — Organic Chemistry**
- **CHEM 211 — UBC-CHEM-211 — Introduction to Chemical Analysis**
- **CHEM 213 — Organic Chemistry**
- **CHEM 245 — UBC-CHEM-245 — Intermediate Organic Chemistry Lab**
- Computing/statistics alternative: **STAT 201 — UBC-STAT-201 — Statistical Inference for Data Science** or **CPSC 203 — UBC-CPSC-203 — Programming, Problem Solving, and Algorithms**

**Year 3 – BCIT**
- **FSCT 8150 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Theory**
- **FSCT 8155 — Forensic Biology: Evidence Recovery**
- **FSCT 8370 — Quality Assurance for Forensic Science**
- **FSCT 8371 — Business Management for Forensic Science**
- Elective pool includes **FSCT 7310 — Crime and Incident Scene Investigation**, **FSCT 7910 — Research Methodology and Measurement Models**, **FSCT 8230 — The Medicolegal Aspects of Alcohol**, **FSCT 8240 — Forensic Toxicology**, and **FSCT 8320 — The Science of Fingerprints - Theory**

**Year 3 – UBC**
- **BIOC 301 — UBC-BIOC-301 — Biochemistry Laboratory**
- **BIOC 303 — UBC-BIOC-303 — Molecular Biochemistry**
- **BIOL 335 — UBC-BIOL-335 — Molecular Genetics**

**Year 4 – BCIT**
- **FSCT 7009 — Law for Forensic Science**
- **FSCT 7010 — The Expert Witness: Prepared for Court**
- **FSCT 8156 — Instrumental Analysis for Forensic Chemistry**
- **FSCT 8160 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Applications**

**Year 4 – UBC**
You choose one of the stored Biochemistry pathways:

- **Path 1:** **BIOC 449 — UBC-BIOC-449 — Honours Thesis** plus 3 credits of advanced Biochemistry electives.
- **Path 2:** **BIOC 420 — UBC-BIOC-420 — Advanced Biochemical Techniques** plus 6 credits of advanced Biochemistry electives.

The advanced Biochemistry options include **BIOC 402 — UBC-BIOC-402 — Proteins: Structure and Function**, **BIOC 403 — UBC-BIOC-403 — Enzymology**, **BIOC 410 — UBC-BIOC-410 — Nucleic Acid: Structure and Function**, **BIOC 421 — UBC-BIOC-421 — Recombinant DNA Techniques**, **BIOC 430 — UBC-BIOC-430 — Advanced Topics in Protein Biochemistry**, **BIOC 440 — UBC-BIOC-440 — Concepts in Molecular Biology**, **BIOC 450 — UBC-BIOC-450 — Membrane Biochemistry**, **BIOC 460 — UBC-BIOC-460 — Advanced Techniques in Biochemistry**, and **BIOC 470 — UBC-BIOC-470 — Biochemistry and Society: Current Issues**.

Other Year 4 UBC options include **BIOL 301 — UBC-BIOL-301 — Biomathematics**, **BIOL 336 — UBC-BIOL-336 — Fundamentals of Evolutionary Biology**, **BIOL 462 — UBC-BIOL-462 — Ecological Plant Biochemistry**, **CPSC 330 — UBC-CPSC-330 — Applied Machine Learning**, **MEDG 421 — UBC-MEDG-421 — Genetics and Cell Biology of Cancer**, **MICB 405 — UBC-MICB-405 — Bioinformatics**, and **PCTH 325 — UBC-PCTH-325 — Rational Basis of Drug Therapy**.

### Admissions information
The stored program record includes:
- A UBC pathway with a minimum GPA of **76%**, changing to **70% for September 2026**, plus specified Chemistry, Communication, Biology, and calculus preparation.
- A transfer pathway requiring two terms of Chemistry with lab, and one term each of Biology, English, and differential calculus.
- A criminal record check as an entrance requirement.
- Optional co-op placement.

The stored admissions record says applications are made through UBC Science/UBC Admissions, followed by an application for the specialization in June. Timing details for the criminal record check are not verified in the available data.

I’ll keep **Combined Honours in Biochemistry and Forensic Science** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor of Science  
- **Duration:** Four years  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Locations:** Burnaby Campus and UBC Vancouver  
- **Institutions:** Joint UBC/BCIT program  
- **Status:** Active  
- **Completion requirement:** 132 credits  

### Curriculum highlights

**Year 1 – UBC**
- Required: **BIOL 112 — UBC-BIOL-112 — Biology of the Cell**
- Required: **CHEM 123 — UBC-CHEM-123 — UBC-CHEM-111 — UBC-CHEM-121 — UBC-CHEM-141 — Principles of Chemistry 2**
- Required: **SCIE 113 — UBC-SCIE-113 — First-Year Seminar in Science**
- Chemistry alternative: **CHEM 121 — Principles of Chemistry**, **CHEM 111 — Principles of Chemistry**, or **CHEM 141 — Principles of Chemistry**, together with **CHEM 123 — Principles of Chemistry 2**
- Data science alternative: **DSCI 100 — UBC-DSCI-100 — Introduction to Data Science** or **CPSC 103 — UBC-CPSC-103 — Introduction to Systematic Program Design**
- Calculus alternative: **MATH 100 — UBC-MATH-100 — UBC-MATH-102 — UBC-MATH-104 — Differential Calculus**, **MATH 102 — Differential Calculus**, or **MATH 104 — Differential Calculus**

**Year 2 – BCIT**
- **COMM 7200 — Report Writing and Workplace Communication for Forensic Investigation**
- **FSCT 7320 — Introduction to Forensic Science**
- **LIBS 7020 — Bioethics**

**Year 2 – UBC**
- Required: **BIOC 203 — UBC-BIOC-203 — Fundamentals of Biochemistry**
- **BIOL 200 — UBC-BIOL-200 — Fundamentals of Cell Biology**
- **BIOL 234 — UBC-BIOL-234 — Fundamentals of Genetics**
- **CHEM 203 — UBC-CHEM-203 — Introduction to UBC-CHEM-213 — Organic Chemistry**
- **CHEM 211 — UBC-CHEM-211 — Introduction to Chemical Analysis**
- **CHEM 213 — Organic Chemistry**
- **CHEM 245 — UBC-CHEM-245 — Intermediate Organic Chemistry Lab**
- Computing/statistics alternative: **STAT 201 — UBC-STAT-201 — Statistical Inference for Data Science** or **CPSC 203 — UBC-CPSC-203 — Programming, Problem Solving, and Algorithms**

**Year 3 – BCIT**
- **FSCT 8150 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Theory**
- **FSCT 8155 — Forensic Biology: Evidence Recovery**
- **FSCT 8370 — Quality Assurance for Forensic Science**
- **FSCT 8371 — Business Management for Forensic Science**
- Elective pool includes **FSCT 7310 — Crime and Incident Scene Investigation**, **FSCT 7910 — Research Methodology and Measurement Models**, **FSCT 8230 — The Medicolegal Aspects of Alcohol**, **FSCT 8240 — Forensic Toxicology**, and **FSCT 8320 — The Science of Fingerprints - Theory**

**Year 3 – UBC**
- **BIOC 301 — UBC-BIOC-301 — Biochemistry Laboratory**
- **BIOC 303 — UBC-BIOC-303 — Molecular Biochemistry**
- **BIOL 335 — UBC-BIOL-335 — Molecular Genetics**

**Year 4 – BCIT**
- **FSCT 7009 — Law for Forensic Science**
- **FSCT 7010 — The Expert Witness: Prepared for Court**
- **FSCT 8156 — Instrumental Analysis for Forensic Chemistry**
- **FSCT 8160 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Applications**

**Year 4 – UBC**
You choose one of the stored Biochemistry pathways:

- **Path 1:** **BIOC 449 — UBC-BIOC-449 — Honours Thesis** plus 3 credits of advanced Biochemistry electives.
- **Path 2:** **BIOC 420 — UBC-BIOC-420 — Advanced Biochemical Techniques** plus 6 credits of advanced Biochemistry electives.

The advanced Biochemistry options include **BIOC 402 — UBC-BIOC-402 — Proteins: Structure and Function**, **BIOC 403 — UBC-BIOC-403 — Enzymology**, **BIOC 410 — UBC-BIOC-410 — Nucleic Acid: Structure and Function**, **BIOC 421 — UBC-BIOC-421 — Recombinant DNA Techniques**, **BIOC 430 — UBC-BIOC-430 — Advanced Topics in Protein Biochemistry**, **BIOC 440 — UBC-BIOC-440 — Concepts in Molecular Biology**, **BIOC 450 — UBC-BIOC-450 — Membrane Biochemistry**, **BIOC 460 — UBC-BIOC-460 — Advanced Techniques in Biochemistry**, and **BIOC 470 — UBC-BIOC-470 — Biochemistry and Society: Current Issues**.

Other Year 4 UBC options include **BIOL 301 — UBC-BIOL-301 — Biomathematics**, **BIOL 336 — UBC-BIOL-336 — Fundamentals of Evolutionary Biology**, **BIOL 462 — UBC-BIOL-462 — Ecological Plant Biochemistry**, **CPSC 330 — UBC-CPSC-330 — Applied Machine Learning**, **MEDG 421 — UBC-MEDG-421 — Genetics and Cell Biology of Cancer**, **MICB 405 — UBC-MICB-405 — Bioinformatics**, and **PCTH 325 — UBC-PCTH-325 — Rational Basis of Drug Therapy**.

The stored program record includes:
- A UBC pathway with a minimum GPA of **76%**, changing to **70% for September 2026**, plus specified Chemistry, Communication, Biology, and calculus preparation.

- A criminal record check as an entrance requirement.
- Optional co-op placement.

I’ll keep **Combined Honours in Biochemistry and Forensic Science** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor of Science  
- **Duration:** Four years  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Locations:** Burnaby Campus and UBC Vancouver  
- **Institutions:** Joint UBC/BCIT program  
- **Status:** Active  
- **Completion requirement:** 132 credits  

### Curriculum highlights

**Year 1 – UBC**
- Required: **BIOL 112 — UBC-BIOL-112 — Biology of the Cell**
- Required: **CHEM 123 — UBC-CHEM-123 — UBC-CHEM-111 — UBC-CHEM-121 — UBC-CHEM-141 — Principles of Chemistry 2**
- Required: **SCIE 113 — UBC-SCIE-113 — First-Year Seminar in Science**
- Chemistry alternative: **CHEM 121 — Principles of Chemistry**, **CHEM 111 — Principles of Chemistry**, or **CHEM 141 — Principles of Chemistry**, together with **CHEM 123 — Principles of Chemistry 2**
- Data science alternative: **DSCI 100 — UBC-DSCI-100 — Introduction to Data Science** or **CPSC 103 — UBC-CPSC-103 — Introduction to Systematic Program Design**
- Calculus alternative: **MATH 100 — UBC-MATH-100 — UBC-MATH-102 — UBC-MATH-104 — Differential Calculus**, **MATH 102 — Differential Calculus**, or **MATH 104 — Differential Calculus**

**Year 2 – BCIT**
- **COMM 7200 — Report Writing and Workplace Communication for Forensic Investigation**
- **FSCT 7320 — Introduction to Forensic Science**
- **LIBS 7020 — Bioethics**

**Year 2 – UBC**
- Required: **BIOC 203 — UBC-BIOC-203 — Fundamentals of Biochemistry**
- **BIOL 200 — UBC-BIOL-200 — Fundamentals of Cell Biology**
- **BIOL 234 — UBC-BIOL-234 — Fundamentals of Genetics**
- **CHEM 203 — UBC-CHEM-203 — Introduction to UBC-CHEM-213 — Organic Chemistry**
- **CHEM 211 — UBC-CHEM-211 — Introduction to Chemical Analysis**
- **CHEM 213 — Organic Chemistry**
- **CHEM 245 — UBC-CHEM-245 — Intermediate Organic Chemistry Lab**
- Computing/statistics alternative: **STAT 201 — UBC-STAT-201 — Statistical Inference for Data Science** or **CPSC 203 — UBC-CPSC-203 — Programming, Problem Solving, and Algorithms**

**Year 3 – BCIT**
- **FSCT 8150 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Theory**
- **FSCT 8155 — Forensic Biology: Evidence Recovery**

- **FSCT 8371 — Business Management for Forensic Science**
- Elective pool includes **FSCT 7310 — Crime and Incident Scene Investigation**, **FSCT 7910 — Research Methodology and Measurement Models**, **FSCT 8230 — The Medicolegal Aspects of Alcohol**, **FSCT 8240 — Forensic Toxicology**, and **FSCT 8320 — The Science of Fingerprints - Theory**

**Year 3 – UBC**
- **BIOC 301 — UBC-BIOC-301 — Biochemistry Laboratory**
- **BIOC 303 — UBC-BIOC-303 — Molecular Biochemistry**
- **BIOL 335 — UBC-BIOL-335 — Molecular Genetics**

**Year 4 – BCIT**
- **FSCT 7009 — Law for Forensic Science**
- **FSCT 7010 — The Expert Witness: Prepared for Court**
- **FSCT 8156 — Instrumental Analysis for Forensic Chemistry**
- **FSCT 8160 — Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Applications**

**Year 4 – UBC**
You choose one of the stored Biochemistry pathways:

- **Path 1:** **BIOC 449 — UBC-BIOC-449 — Honours Thesis** plus 3 credits of advanced Biochemistry electives.
- **Path 2:** **BIOC 420 — UBC-BIOC-420 — Advanced Biochemical Techniques** plus 6 credits of advanced Biochemistry electives.

The advanced Biochemistry options include **BIOC 402 — UBC-BIOC-402 — Proteins: Structure and Function**, **BIOC 403 — UBC-BIOC-403 — Enzymology**, **BIOC 410 — UBC-BIOC-410 — Nucleic Acid: Structure and Function**, **BIOC 421 — UBC-BIOC-421 — Recombinant DNA Techniques**, **BIOC 430 — UBC-BIOC-430 — Advanced Topics in Protein Biochemistry**, **BIOC 440 — UBC-BIOC-440 — Concepts in Molecular Biology**, **BIOC 450 — UBC-BIOC-450 — Membrane Biochemistry**, **BIOC 460 — UBC-BIOC-460 — Advanced Techniques in Biochemistry**, and **BIOC 470 — UBC-BIOC-470 — Biochemistry and Society: Current Issues**.

Other Year 4 UBC options include **BIOL 301 — UBC-BIOL-301 — Biomathematics**, **BIOL 336 — UBC-BIOL-336 — Fundamentals of Evolutionary Biology**, **BIOL 462 — UBC-BIOL-462 — Ecological Plant Biochemistry**, **CPSC 330 — UBC-CPSC-330 — Applied Machine Learning**, **MEDG 421 — UBC-MEDG-421 — Genetics and Cell Biology of Cancer**, **MICB 405 — UBC-MICB-405 — Bioinformatics**, and **PCTH 325 — UBC-PCTH-325 — Rational Basis of Drug Therapy**.

### Admissions information

- A transfer pathway requiring two terms of Chemistry with lab, and one term each of Biology, English, and differential calculus.

The **Combined Honours in Biochemistry and Forensic Science** is a **four-year, full-time Bachelor of Science** jointly delivered by **UBC and BCIT**, with study at UBC Vancouver and BCIT’s Burnaby campus.

[View the program information and source](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/)
Where would I study?

You would study at **both BCIT’s Burnaby Campus and UBC Vancouver**. The program is delivered **in person**.

[View the program information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/)

expectation.question: What should I know before applying?

response.answer:
Before applying to the **Combined Honours in Biochemistry and Forensic Science, Bachelor of Science**, keep these points in mind:

### Program basics
- It is a **four-year, full-time** program delivered in person at **UBC Vancouver and BCIT’s Burnaby Campus**.
- The program leads to a **Bachelor of Science** and requires **132 credits**.
- A **co-op placement is optional**.

### Admission pathways

**UBC pathway**
The stored requirements indicate:

- Minimum GPA of **76%**; for the **September 2026 intake**, the stored exception is **70%**.
- **8.0 credits of UBC Chemistry**, consisting of **CHEM 121 – UBC-CHEM-111 — UBC-CHEM-121 — UBC-CHEM-141 — Principles of Chemistry** or **CHEM 111 – Principles of Chemistry** or **CHEM 141 – Principles of Chemistry**, plus **CHEM 123 – UBC-CHEM-123 — Principles of Chemistry 2**.
- **3.0 credits** satisfying the UBC Communication Requirement.
- **BIOL 112 – UBC-BIOL-112 — Biology of the Cell**.
- **3.0 credits of UBC-MATH-100 — UBC-MATH-102 — UBC-MATH-104 — Differential Calculus**.

**Transfer pathway**
The stored description indicates:

- Two terms of Chemistry with lab.
- One term each of Biology, English, and differential calculus.
- The pathway record also specifies a **76% minimum GPA**; the September 2026 exception is recorded separately as **70%**.

### Other entrance information
- A **criminal record check** is listed as an entrance requirement. The timing is not verified in the available data.
- Applications are recorded as being made through **UBC Science/UBC Admissions**, followed by an application for the specialization in June for eligible students. This workflow requires confirmation with UBC.
- For international applicants, the available record indicates that the program is available for application and marked **PGWP eligible to apply**, but study-permit information is not published in the stored data.

### What still needs confirmation
Your eligibility cannot be determined without knowing your GPA, completed coursework, pathway, intake, and—if applicable—international status. The institution should confirm course equivalencies, the application sequence, criminal-record-check timing, and current deadlines.

[View the program information and source](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/)

- A **co-op placement is optional**.

**UBC pathway**
The stored requirements indicate:

- Minimum GPA of **76%**; for the **September 2026 intake**, the stored exception is **70%**.

- **3.0 credits** satisfying the UBC Communication Requirement.
- **BIOL 112 – Biology of the Cell**.
- **3.0 credits of differential calculus**.

**Transfer pathway**
The stored description indicates:

- Two terms of Chemistry with lab.
- One term each of Biology, English, and differential calculus.

For an admissions scenario, inspect the resolved program's structured ADMISSION and INTERNATIONAL rules. Separate requirements directly met by the student's stated facts, facts still missing, and non-executable or institutionally verified requirements needing human confirmation; never invent an unstored requirement. Category questions must search programs by credential. An explicit whole-catalog question overrides all prior or selected program context; report its count, program list, or distinct credentials only from the search_programs result. Progress percentages must be quoted only from the program-progress tool and never calculated from level numbers. If requested detail is missing and a verified source_url exists, provide that link as the fallback. For international applicants, the program record indicates that it is **available for application** and **eligible to apply for a post-graduation work permit (PGWP)**.

- A criminal record check, with timing not verified in the stored data

It is a **full-time** program. It takes four years and is delivered in person at **BCIT’s Burnaby Campus and UBC Vancouver**.

Before applying to the **Combined Honours in Biochemistry and Forensic Science, Bachelor of Science**, keep these points in mind:

### Program basics
- It is a **four-year, full-time** program delivered in person at **UBC Vancouver and BCIT’s Burnaby Campus**.
- The program leads to a **Bachelor of Science** and requires **132 credits**.
- A **co-op placement is optional**.

### Admission pathways

**UBC pathway**
The stored requirements indicate:

- Minimum GPA of **76%**; for the **September 2026 intake**, the stored exception is **70%**.
- **8.0 credits of UBC Chemistry**, consisting of **CHEM 121 – UBC-CHEM-111 — UBC-CHEM-121 — UBC-CHEM-141 — Principles of Chemistry** or **CHEM 111 – Principles of Chemistry** or **CHEM 141 – Principles of Chemistry**, plus **CHEM 123 – UBC-CHEM-123 — Principles of Chemistry 2**.
- **3.0 credits** satisfying the UBC Communication Requirement.
- **BIOL 112 – UBC-BIOL-112 — Biology of the Cell**.
- **3.0 credits of UBC-MATH-100 — UBC-MATH-102 — UBC-MATH-104 — Differential Calculus**.

**Transfer pathway**
The stored description indicates:

- Two terms of Chemistry with lab.
- One term each of Biology, English, and differential calculus.
- The pathway record also specifies a **76% minimum GPA**; the September 2026 exception is recorded separately as **70%**.

conversation.content: Is it online or in person?

It is **in person**, with classes at **BCIT’s Burnaby Campus and UBC Vancouver**.

[View the program information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/)
Is it full-time or part-time?

It is a **full-time** program. It takes four years and is delivered in person at **BCIT’s Burnaby Campus and UBC Vancouver**.

[View the program information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/)
What should I know before applying?

Before applying to the **Combined Honours in Biochemistry and Forensic Science, Bachelor of Science**, keep these points in mind:

### Program basics
- It is a **four-year, full-time** program delivered in person at **UBC Vancouver and BCIT’s Burnaby Campus**.
- The program leads to a **Bachelor of Science** and requires **132 credits**.
- A **co-op placement is optional**.

### Admission pathways

**UBC pathway**
The stored requirements indicate:

- Minimum GPA of **76%**; for the **September 2026 intake**, the stored exception is **70%**.
- **8.0 credits of UBC Chemistry**, consisting of **CHEM 121 – UBC-CHEM-111 — UBC-CHEM-121 — UBC-CHEM-141 — Principles of Chemistry** or **CHEM 111 – Principles of Chemistry** or **CHEM 141 – Principles of Chemistry**, plus **CHEM 123 – UBC-CHEM-123 — Principles of Chemistry 2**.
- **3.0 credits** satisfying the UBC Communication Requirement.
- **BIOL 112 – UBC-BIOL-112 — Biology of the Cell**.
- **3.0 credits of UBC-MATH-100 — UBC-MATH-102 — UBC-MATH-104 — Differential Calculus**.

**Transfer pathway**
The stored description indicates:

- Two terms of Chemistry with lab.
- One term each of Biology, English, and differential calculus.
- The pathway record also specifies a **76% minimum GPA**; the September 2026 exception is recorded separately as **70%**.

### Other entrance information
- A **criminal record check** is listed as an entrance requirement. The timing is not verified in the available data.
- Applications are recorded as being made through **UBC Science/UBC Admissions**, followed by an application for the specialization in June for eligible students. This workflow requires confirmation with UBC.
- For international applicants, the available record indicates that the program is available for application and marked **PGWP eligible to apply**, but study-permit information is not published in the stored data.

### What still needs confirmation
Your eligibility cannot be determined without knowing your GPA, completed coursework, pathway, intake, and—if applicable—international status. The institution should confirm course equivalencies, the application sequence, criminal-record-check timing, and current deadlines.

[View the program information and source](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/)
What about international applicants?

For international applicants, the program record indicates that it is **available for application** and **eligible to apply for a post-graduation work permit (PGWP)**.

However, the available Asteris data does **not** publish study-permit requirements or other international-specific admission requirements. Please confirm those details with BCIT/UBC and Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC).

The program’s general admission pathways still list requirements such as:

- Minimum GPA of **76%**; **70% for the September 2026 intake**
- Required chemistry, biology, communication, and differential-calculus coursework, depending on the pathway
- A criminal record check, with timing not verified in the stored data

[View the program information and international applicant source](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/combined-honours-in-biochemistry-and-forensic-science-bachelor-of-science-full-time-9940bsc/)  
[BCIT international applicants](https://www.bcit.ca/international-applicants/regular-credential-programs/)

Describe it as courses the student told you they completed; never mention or imply an academic profile or stored student record. Spanish When a student-supplied numeric fact can be compared directly with a verified minimum, give the deterministic result and the exact difference. Qualify only whether the stated experience or credential meets the stored definition; do not say the result cannot be verified and then state the rule. Describe CMGT 8700 generically as requiring completion of required program coursework before the student's chosen final-project course; never describe CMGT 8800 as the only possible final project. Credit-based elective rules are MINIMUM_CREDITS_FROM_POOL rules, not course-count rules. Describe them as completing at least the stated credits from the approved pool. Never infer a fixed number of courses or assume every option has equal credits. Use choose-N wording only when a structured choice group provides a choose count. For every structured OR or choice group, clearly say the student chooses one option; never turn alternatives into cumulative requirements or call the set optional. A required A-or-B set is a graduation requirement even though each individual branch is an alternative. Keep ADMISSION/ENTRANCE rules separate from GRADUATION/CURRICULUM rules and never use one to answer the other. For graduation questions, call evaluate_program_curriculum when available and prefer it over individual course role labels. Department approval applies to CMGT 8800 and CMGT 8810, not CMGT 8700. CMGT 8700 itself requires the stored coursework-completion rule, two years of related work experience, an industry topic, and an industry sponsor. The standard Liberal Studies component totals 12 credits. For part-time students, explain that LIBS 7013 may be replaced by one additional 3-credit Liberal Studies elective while the other Liberal Studies requirements remain; do not call a replaceable course mandatory. A resolved active program is authoritative for every program-specific tool. Never substitute a different program because a search is empty or irrelevant. Never invent application, acceptance, reapplication, enrolment, or document timing. For a current student asking about another pathway, explain only stored pathway and curriculum facts; label unstored transition or reapplication rules unknown. Answer yes/no and discovery questions concisely unless the student asks to list, show, browse, compare, or explain. Clearly label any inference, or omit it. uses exactly the same tools and rules as English. Respond entirely in the language of the current student question: English. Conversation history may provide subject or entity context but must never determine or carry over the response language. Keep co-op work terms, practical-work hours, and academic level progression separate. A level explicitly named in the current question overrides unrelated levels in history; never offer progression to another level.
